findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Inspectors observed the Certified Food Manager Certificate (CFM) on file to have expired in March of last year. The person in charge (PIC) stated that they have not retaken the test since then. Inspector provided PIC with a handout on accredited institutes through which they may retake the exam. A CFM must be on site at all times during which food is being prepared or handled. The presence of a CFM helps to oversee proper food handling and cold holding temperatures to ensure facility is in compliance with safe food handling and preparation. Retake the test by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 
During today’s visit inspectors observed multiple items in the hand sink. PIC was made aware and Items were removed. Ensure that the hand sink is available for hand washing at all times. 

Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspector observed mouse dropping next to a bag of wheat flour in the facility’s dry storage area. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) cleaned the area immediately. Ensure the facility is cleaned on a routine basis to eliminate conditions for pest harborage.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions. [C]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.citation_text:
3-305.11(A) 
Multiple cardboard boxes of food items were observed store directly on the floor in different areas in the facility. PIC was informed. PIC assured inspectors that the boxes will be removed from the floor. Ensure that food items stored at least 6 inches above the floor to protect them from form splash, dust, or other contamination.

Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
6-101.11(A)
Inspectors observed ice accumulation in multiple Chest sliding freezer. Discussed with PIC. PIC stated Ice accumulation will be clean. Ensure that Ice is cleaned to provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface. 

(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
The PIC was unable to produce Food Handlers Certificates during today’s inspection. Discussed with PIC. PIC stated inspected that training will be done soon. Ensure all workers who handle or prepare food have and maintain their Food Handler’s Certificate every 3 years. Food Handler’s must have a certificate on file within 30 days of hire. Ensure these documents are available upon request during future inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple items (pork belly, Mackerel, Tilapia) to have torn packaging, or be outside of their packaging in the sliding chest coolers & freezers. CORRECTED- items were re-wrapped. Ensure all temperature control for safety (TCS) food items that are packaged on site retain their seal to protect against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.[Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed the sliding chest cooler in front of the food prep area to not contain an ambient thermometer. CORRECTED- the PIC added an ambient thermometer to the cooling unit. Ensure all cooling units contain an ambient thermometer to measure the temperature at the warmest part of the cooling unit. This helps the facility ensure all cooling units are working properly to hold items at 41F or below.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT: 1) Inspectors observed mouse droppings on the floor and between boxes in the back dry storage area (shipping container). 
2) Inspector also observed a dead bug on a noodle package on the top shelf of the open air cooler. CORRECTED- this item was removed from service by the PIC.

The facility uses Sonny Adams for Pest Control once monthly. Droppings should be cleaned up, but large pallets of food will need to be moved to properly clean. Contact pest control operator, and monitor the area for evidence of pest after clean up, and check shipments for pests during delivery.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed a significant amount of brown rice being stored in a cardboard box, with an open top in the back dry storage area. Foods in dry storage should be completely covered in a food-grade package or container to prevent the contamination of food. This storage method also may attract pests (see violation #38). Ensure foods are protected from contamination during storage.
findings.citation_text: 3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

See that hot water is always available. A new hot water heater was just installed and hot water was able to be supplied during the inspection.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Quail eggs were observed in a double door cooler above kimchi and other packaged items. CORRECTED- Storage was rearranged to keep quail eggs below packaged foods. 
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. [P]

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
1st  REPEAT: No ambient thermometer is present in the 2 door cooler. CORRECTED- PIC added a thermometer to the cooler. 
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. [C]

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.comment:
Repackaged frozen meats observed in two chest freezers without appropriate labeling. The facility has been able to properly label multiple foods, there remains some whole, intact fish that need proper cooking instructions (the common name is indicated on the freezer holding the foods. See that cooking instructions are available either on the packaging OR simply print a label to affix to the front of the freezer.  

3-602.11: (A) FOOD PACKAGED in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be properly labeled. (B) Regulatory requirements-(1) The common name of the FOOD/identity statement; 106 (2) List ingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, declaration of artificial colors and flavors and chemical preservatives; (3) net contents; (4) The name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor; and (5) MAJOR FOOD ALLERGENS. (6) Nutrition labeling as specified in 21 CFR 101 - Food Labeling and 9 CFR 317 Subpart B Nutrition Labeling UNLESS EXEMPT Under FDCA. (Pf) (C) Bulk FOOD for CONSUMER self-dispensing shall be labeled in plain view. (D) Bulk, unPACKAGED FOODS portioned for CONSUMERS shall be properly labeled. [C]

There are still a very small number of mouse droppings observed in the far back storage area. Droppings are minimal and may be easily cleaned BUT pallets of bulk foods will need to be moved in-order to properly clean. Continue to provide regular PCO service and monitor and clean when activity is observed.  No damaged packaging is observed. 

The facility will be given thirty days to inspect to allow ample time for proper cleaning. 
PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.comment:
4-303.11: There is no bleach available within the store. The facility does minimal processing and does not immediately need the sanitizer. See that bleach is provided and that the available test strips are used to determine the proper concentration (100-200ppm).

(A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: There is pressed wood shelving over the triple sink that is unsealed. Properly seal/paint the shelves so the surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable. Also, a couple of the reach-in freezers are observed to have significant ice accumulation. Defrost the freezers so they are able to be easily cleaned. 
Also, there is cardboard being used on the top of a roll cart adjacent to the wrapping station. See that the cardboard is removed and replaced with a cleanable surfaces (think plastic sheet). The cardboard is protecting over single-service items. The cardboard is starting to show signs of wear and should be replaced with a suitable alternative.  

(A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
4-101.16:  The facility is using sponges to wash, rinse, and sanitize utensils. Cease use of sponges and switch to a cloth that can be properly laundered between uses. Facility was educated on proper ware washing and use of materials for the task. Demonstrated use of bleach and test strips too. Facility truly only uses a small amount of equipment for cutting of fruits and meat. Discussed washing-in-place of the saw blade. 
Sponges may not be used in contact with cleaned and SANITIZED or in-use FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES. [C]

findings.title: Garbage & refuse properly disposed; facilities maintained
findings.comment:
There is no garbage can present at the prep area handwashing sink. Provide a trash can for disposal of paper towels.
5-501.16: (C) A waste receptacle shall be located at each lavatory if disposable towels are used. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 Owner took food manager course through SCDPH in March 2020 but does not have a copy of certification. Owner was advised on process to obtain a copy of the CFM certificate (see general comments for details). 
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 Wood was painted at the partition installed at the meat packing area. Gaps remain to be sealed along edges of wood and plastic covering on the outside along the aisle. 
-Ceiling of the entryway and the area outside the building where the metal carton and the building meet have not yet been repaired to eliminate entrance of rainwater into the building. It was not raining at the time of inspection, so leaking rainwater was not an issue. Owner was advised to get the necessary repairs completed to minimize leaking rainwater during future weather events. 
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Proof of food handler certifications were not available for any staff. All staff that are not certified food managers need to complete an online food handler certification course that is ANSI and IL approved. Copies of certifications need to be maintained on-site.
All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Owner has not yet obtained a food manager certification, and several priority violations were observed at the time of inspection. Priority violations included, but were not limited to, a retail cooler knowingly holding above 45F used for storage of TCS foods, lack of handwashing in the meat packaging area, lack of ware washing for food contact surfaces, and proper bleach was not available for use.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 Owner does not have a food manager certification. Owner noted a food manager course and exam were completed through SCDPH in 2019, but owner never received results or the certification. Owner was provided with information to contact ServSafe to follow-up on certification.
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) Owner could not locate employee health policy documents provided and discussed during previous routine inspection. Copies of signed reporting agreements were not available for the owner and his staff. Revised versions of employee health documents were provided on new letterhead with updated reference to 2017 FDA Food Code and discussed. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring, and maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for all staff. 
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.citation_text:
2-501.11 Written procedure with specific actions to be taken in case of a vomit and/or diarrhea incident was not available. Norovirus disinfection handout was provided and discussed. Bleach is available for use. Maintain the norovirus disinfection policy on-site along with all other employee health documentation.
A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.11 Handwashing could not occur at meat packaging area as needed between tasks because the handwashing sink was blocked. Proper handwashing between tasks and ensuring access to allow proper handwashing were discussed. An employee was later observed washing hands at the designated handwashing sink when it was accessible. 
Food employees shall keep their hands and exposed portions of their arms clean.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Upon arrival handwashing sink in packaging area was blocked. Foam trays were observed in the basin, and trays with meat that were waiting to be wrapped were balanced along the edge of the handwashing sink. Employee working in the area was advised on proper use of the handwashing sink. All items were removed to allow for access to the handwashing sink.
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease the practice of placing items in the basin and along the outer edge of the handsink.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11 Cartons of raw quail eggs were stored above cheese and bread in a retail cooler. Proper storage of raw animal foods was discussed. Eggs were discarded due to improper holding temperature (see #22 & 33 for details).
Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods from ready to eat foods during storage, preparation, holding, and display.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 While discussing the cleaning procedure for the meat saw, owner stated the saw is cleaned at the end of the day using only hot water. Owner was advised that all food contact surfaces (any surface that food comes in contact with during use) must be manually washed with hot soapy water, rinsed with clean water, and then sanitized with a bleach solution. Owner stated he understood and moving forward the meat saw would be properly washed, rinsed, and sanitized between uses. 
Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned after use.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-702.11 A proper sanitizer was not available for use. Lemon scented bleach and an unopened ammonia chloride disinfectant were observed in the meat packaging area. Bleach was purchased during inspection. Ensure proper sanitization of all food contact surfaces. 
Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be sanitized before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 TCS foods in the 2 door retail cooler had internal temperatures at 46F-52F. Foods included yogurt (48.5F), multiple packages of tofu (46.5F-51.5F), soy puffs (50F), and quail eggs (52F). Foods in question were discarded in the dumpster during inspection. Photos were taken, and a voluntary order of destruction was generated.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-204.11 A small bottle of lemon scented bleach was observed in the meat packaging area. Proper use of approved sanitizers was discussed. No more cutting or packaging of products could occur until proper bleach was provided. Bleach was purchased during the inspection. Owner was advised to maintain all bleach solutions at 200ppm as required by the product label directions.
Chemical sanitizers, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to food contact surfaces shall meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions).

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
4-301.11 Two door retail cooler was holding above 45F. Digital thermostat was observed at 46F. Inspector placed thermometers in the cooler and observed temperatures at 48F-50F. Owner noted the cooler digital thermostat was reading at 46F for the last couple of weeks and that service was needed. All TCS foods were discarded during inspection (see #22 for details). Owner put a call in for service. Owner was advised the cooler cold not be used for storage of any TCS food until it is able to maintain foods at 41F/below. Owner stated he understood. 
Equipment holding cold food shall be sufficient in number and capacity to maintain proper temperature of TCS foods.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13 Boxes of frozen fish that needed to be separated and portioned prior to being placed in retail freezers were sitting on the floor at room temperate. Owner noted the fish was previously stored in the walk-in freezer but removed to allow fish to thaw slightly so products could be easily separated during portioning. Proper thawing was discussed, and boxes of fish were placed in the walk-in cooler.
TCS food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration at 41°F/below; (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F/below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-305.14 Fly strip was observed hanging in the middle of the meat packaging area. Fly strip was removed and discarded at request of inspector. Owner was advised on proper placement of fly strips in the future. Ensure fly strips are not placed directly above meat packaging. 
Unpackaged food shall be protected from environmental sources of contamination during prep.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-305.11 Bags of onions were on the floor in the walkin cooler. Several boxes of produce and other foods were also observed on the floor in the walk-in cooler and in the store. Proper storage at least 6 inches off the floor was discussed.
Food shall be protected from contamination by storing food at least 6 inches above the floor.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-202.16 Freezer used for storage of banana leaves and other items had heavy ice buildup, and old, damaged cardboard boxes used as partitions between foods. Defrost the freezer and remove old cardboard. Cease the practice of using cardboard in freezers and provide additional hard plastic dividers similar to those observed in other freezers. 
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 Sanitizer solution was not available for use in meat packaging area while employee was working. Ensure sanitizer solution is prepared and available for use when working in the meat packaging area. 
Sanitizer shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 Rain water was leaking in at the entryway between the store and the back storage area. Metal containers were used to catch dripping water. Get the ceiling of the entryway and the area outside the building where the metal carton and the building meet repaired to eliminate entrance of rainwater into the building. 
-A new partition with wood and plexiglass has been installed at the meat packing area. Raw wood needs to be painted, and all gaps between wood need to be sealed with caulk.
-WALK-IN FREEZER - 1. Piece of wood at the threshold was loose. Seal the wood to the floor. 2. Foam insulation was exposed around the doorframe inside the walkin freezer. Seal the inner doorframe of the walk-in freezer. 
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Proof of food handler certifications were not available for any staff. All staff that are not certified food managers need to complete an online food handler certification course that is ANSI and IL approved. Copies of certifications need to be maintained on-site.
All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.
